institution: Smithsonian National Museum of American History
title: William H. Phinney’s weight-and-price scale patent model
summary: Phinney’s scale model relates measured weight and a posted price. The museum says it was commercially unsuccessful.
limit: A calculation on a patent model leaves actual sales and demand open.
offer: Use the held weight card without changing the marked rate.
check: Reset the marked rate while holding the practice weight fixed.

institution: Smithsonian National Museum of American History
title: Thomas T. Strode’s accounting adding-machine patent model
summary: This patent model puts five turning discs on a paddle marked with one hundred divisions.
limit: The running total cannot supply the origin of the entries on its own.
offer: Put both copied sales into the paper adder to test the displayed total.
check: Trace the two entries back to the single source slip before adding.

institution: Smithsonian National Museum of American History
title: William C. McGill’s cash register patent model
summary: Four numbered wheels in McGill’s model represent different money positions.
limit: A recorded price leaves payment status open until the drawer is checked.
offer: Roll the toy digits to the listed amount.
check: Put a separate payment stub beneath the same dial amount.

institution: Smithsonian National Museum of American History
title: National Cash Register Class 51
summary: A National Cash Register Company model developed for high-volume supermarket checkout.
limit: A fast recorded sale total leaves the choices of people who left the line uncounted.
offer: Check the quick line of registered sales.
check: Put the waiting customers’ named slips in a separate counting pocket.

institution: Smithsonian National Museum of American History
title: Eight-total National Cash Register mechanism
summary: This separate National Cash Register Company component holds the counters for eight totals along one shaft.
limit: A sum needs its counter’s meaning before it can support a claim about customers or revenue.
offer: Move the practice count card to the total it actually belongs to.
check: Match each printed mark to its own counter before checking a combined figure.

institution: Smithsonian National Museum of American History
title: National Cash Register Model 1852-E
summary: The register has a separate column of keys for transaction type and four sets for selecting amounts.
limit: Equal money entries can represent different types of transactions.
offer: Enter the same amount on two practice purchase strips.
check: Leave the amounts in their receipt and reversal columns before totalling.

institution: Smithsonian National Museum of American History
title: Kern merchant bankbook
summary: The title gives John G. Kern. The description and related-name field give John F. Kern, a merchant of Germantown, Ohio. The manuscript records deposits and withdrawals.
limit: The catalogue disagrees on the owner’s middle initial. A remembered deposit and the dated balance also answer different questions.
offer: Keep the last written amount with its account date.
check: Read the deposit and withdrawal lines separately before bringing the new balance forward.

institution: Smithsonian National Museum of American History
title: Coal scrip booklet linked to Black Diamond Collieries
summary: The museum uses this booklet to explain company scrip, which could be used in company stores. Scrip could be issued as wages or credit against wages.
limit: A marked amount has a spending boundary. It cannot stand for access to every store or an independently checked wage.
offer: Keep the practice credit in the named company store’s slot.
check: Test the same slip at the second shop and record where it cannot be used.

institution: Smithsonian National Museum of American History
title: Cocos (Keeling) Islands company-store scrip set
summary: The museum records nine celluloid pieces of the store scrip introduced by the Ross family in 1913. It distinguishes this from legal tender.
limit: The set and its history establish an issuing context. They do not establish whether residents could shop elsewhere with it.
offer: Put a paper token and its named store on one card.
check: Keep the issuing store and a second seller’s accepted payment visibly separate.

institution: Smithsonian National Museum of American History
title: Buxton and Landstreet Company scrip marked 1.00
summary: The 1.00 celluloid disk names the company running stores affiliated with the Davis Coal and Coke Company mines in West Virginia.
limit: The printed number remains tied to its issuer. It does not provide a general legal-tender claim.
offer: Put the figure on the issuing store’s sign with its name.
check: Compare the company drawer with a second merchant’s accepted forms before writing an exchange line.

institution: Smithsonian National Museum of American History
title: Straight’s Shoe Store advertising token
summary: Scovill Manufacturing Company produced this advertising token around 1863.
limit: A token that names a store can direct a customer without proving it paid for a purchase.
offer: Move the store’s name beside the door where a visitor can see it.
check: Leave a transaction blank beside the separately marked advertising token.

institution: Smithsonian National Museum of American History
title: Sample American Express credit card
summary: The museum catalogues this item as a sample card made by American Express.
limit: A sample can illustrate an account instrument without authorizing a purchase.
offer: Put the facing card where a counter worker can compare its sample marks.
check: Set an authorized-use placeholder beside the separate demonstration card.

institution: Smithsonian National Museum of American History
title: Minidoka Consumers’ Cooperative letter to Mr Davidson
summary: The catalogue identifies the Minidoka Consumers’ Cooperative as sender and Mr Davidson as addressee. The National Park Service documents Minidoka as a site where the US incarcerated people of Japanese ancestry during World War II.
limit: The particular correspondence records one administrative contact. It does not speak for everyone held at Minidoka.
offer: Put the sender and recipient in two separate paper pockets.
check: Keep the letter as one dated institutional contact and leave room for a separate individual account.

institution: Smithsonian National Museum of American History
title: Office of Price Administration processed-food ration card
summary: The Smithsonian records a card for processed foods made by the US Office of Price Administration.
limit: A ration card identifies a purchase condition and category. A separate receipt is needed for an actual completed sale.
offer: Clip the practice points to the eligible goods category.
check: Put one redeemed order in its own pocket beside the remaining entitlement.

title: John Baker’s Moorgate swan token
summary: The British Museum records a swan on this dated alloy token issued at Moorgate, London.
limit: A swan can distinguish one trade token. It does not identify all traders named John Baker.
offer: Turn the copied swan mark toward the named Moorgate slot.
check: Compare the issuing place alongside the name shared with another token.

title: Thomas Baker’s Canterbury scales token
summary: The token shows a hand holding scales and names Thomas Baker as issuer in Canterbury.
limit: A sign of weighing is evidence of a mark. It does not certify a particular checked measure.
offer: Put the shop mark where the next buyer can see who issued it.
check: Take the marked promise to a separate paper balance check.

title: Randal Baker’s candle-making token
summary: The copper-alloy token issued in New Street, Shoe Lane shows a person making candles.
limit: An image links the record with a trade. It leaves the volume and value of actual sales open.
offer: Put the candle maker’s mark on the named practice offer.
check: Use a separately checked sale slip before changing the stall’s total.

title: John Legg’s York trade token
summary: The dated York token carries the Bakers’ Arms.
limit: The same trade emblem can appear in more than one shop. The issuing name and place give narrower evidence.
offer: Set the Bakers’ Arms facing outward beside the named York shelf.
check: Add a second issuer key before comparing the two tokens.

title: Dunblane Co-operative Society plastic token
summary: This plastic token was issued by Dunblane Co-operative Society Ltd.
limit: The token records one society’s involvement. Its use at another society is an open question.
offer: Fit the co-operative’s name to its own redemption rail.
check: Try the printed token with a second reader and keep their different response.

title: Rochdale Provident Co-operative Society token
summary: The British Museum names the Rochdale Provident Co-operative Society as issuer of this specific alloy token.
limit: The named issuer supports a claim about this token’s scope. It does not name an individual holder.
offer: Keep the named society beside the token’s printed value.
check: Ask a second mock stall about acceptance under its own rule.

title: Leicester Co-operative Society metal token
summary: The record names Leicester Co-operative Society Ltd as issuer and gives a weight of one gramme.
limit: Weight and denomination are separate measurements. A match on one does not settle the other.
offer: Put both tokens on the marked reference tray with their issuer slips.
check: Compare physical weight and permitted use on separately named lines.

title: Lancaster Banking Company balance book
summary: The catalogue records this dated paper balance book as issued in Lancaster by Lancaster Banking Co.
limit: A dated balance record and a new withdrawal need separate places.
offer: Keep the stated balance beside its source date.
check: Update a practice withdrawal on a new dated line instead of rewriting the old amount.

title: Xuantong-era silver dollar with chopmarks
summary: The Qing silver dollar has a dragon, a bilingual inscription and chopmarks. The British Museum dates its production to 1911.
limit: The original coin issue can be dated. The record leaves the individual people and dates behind the later marks open.
offer: Mount the printed mint date where it remains separate from later marks.
check: Use the later marks as a separate custody clue while keeping their unknown dates visible.

title: Pair of half-unit fuel ration coupons
summary: The British Museum records two connected half-unit fuel ration coupons with printed fields.
limit: An intact sheet shows units available. It does not by itself show a delivery.
offer: Set the two permitted half units beside their designated drawer.
check: Count a single redeemed coupon separately from the allowance still on the sheet.

title: P&O–Orient Lines Cruise Now, Pay Later brochure
summary: The brochure advertised payment options and a reduced fare scheme.
limit: An advertised option does not record which payment arrangement a passenger chose.
offer: Show the advertised lower fare with the brochure issue date.
check: Put a separate payment schedule beside the quoted fare.

title: Bibby Line sailing and fare list for 1932
summary: The museum records this 1931 object as the Bibby Line’s 1932 timetable and fare list.
limit: The issue date gives the publication history. The timetable’s fare applies to its advertised schedule.
offer: Set the labelled 1932 fare window beside the dock date.
check: File the 1931 issue and intended travel year in different slots.

title: A. J. Cater’s Queen Mary passage contract
summary: The contract ticket was issued to A. J. Cater for a Queen Mary sailing and includes payment details.
limit: A named ticket records a booking and stated terms. It leaves actual boarding to a separate record.
offer: Keep the named ticket beside its scheduled departure.
check: Put a boarding verification card in a separate compartment.

title: H. J. Cater’s Queen Elizabeth passage contract
summary: This contract ticket was issued to H. J. Cater for the 8 November 1968 sailing.
limit: A similar surname or ship title leaves the passenger identity and sailing date too uncertain for a transfer.
offer: Check both initials and the exact named sailing on the practice ticket.
check: Attach a separate individual receipt to avoid a same-surname match.

title: London Special Train second-section ticket
summary: The card is for a London Special Train tied to first-class Cunard Queen Elizabeth travel.
limit: Eligibility for one service and a verified rail trip are different records.
offer: Put the relevant service category beside the advertised train time.
check: File a use tick apart from the named passage category.

title: Southern Cross one-way Melbourne–Southampton ticket
summary: A Shaw Savill passage ticket with an insert records one-way travel from Melbourne to Southampton aboard Southern Cross.
limit: The stated trip direction limits which fare comparison is meaningful. It does not establish a return price.
offer: Put the one-way trip direction beside the fare reference.
check: Place a blank for the return trip instead of doubling the original quote.

title: Photowork’s photograph of Mulbera passengers at check-in
summary: The photograph shows passengers checking in at a ticket table inside London’s Royal Albert Dock sheds.
limit: One view of people at a queue leaves the ship’s total travellers and who completed check-in open.
offer: Mark the check-in views visible within the picture’s limits.
check: Ask a separate model clerk to count completed entries outside the picture’s scope.

title: Shopfront from 3 quai de Bourbon
summary: The Met associates the Paris shopfront with Séjournant and notes later replacements.
limit: A later replacement can preserve the shop’s access while leaving the date of each part separate.
offer: Mount the early facade date next to its documented address.
check: Give a replacement panel a different tag before opening the reconstructed counter.

title: Abraham Bosse’s Gallery of the Palace of Justice
summary: Bosse’s print depicts a Paris gallery with different merchants and shoppers, including one person inspecting fans.
limit: Looking at a product does not establish that it was bought or what price was paid.
offer: Move the visible shopper’s browsing token to the display side.
check: Wait for a separately signed practice sale before putting a mark on the sold side.

title: Joachim Beuckelaer’s Fish Market
summary: The Met dates this Fish Market painting to 1568 and identifies Beuckelaer as its maker.
limit: What an artist chooses to show leaves the market’s sale volumes and visitors outside the picture open.
offer: Set the pictured goods beside the painted market’s frame.
check: Use a separately observed market count for a claim about quantities.

title: Inigo Vonholte’s Fine Waters trade card
summary: The Met links this Newcastle-upon-Tyne trade card to Inigo Vonholte’s business and its location at the Key Side.
limit: A card links a product claim with its seller and address. It does not verify an individual purchase.
offer: Post the offer with the vendor’s name so someone can find the place.
check: Put the chosen goods in the payment row only when a separate buyer slip arrives.

title: Francesco Curti’s Trades of Bologna, plate 5
summary: The Met records a plate from Curti’s illustrated series on the trades of Bologna. This sheet depicts several vendors.
limit: A selection of pictured jobs reveals the maker’s representation. It cannot count the whole city’s trades.
offer: Group the pictured trade signs into the printed frame.
check: Keep an open space for the jobs a separate visitor finds outside the frame.
